title: Let him go up (2 Chronicles 36:23)
hook: the Hebrew Bible ends with Cyrus's call to go up and rebuild

segments.voice: Yesterday, Chronicles opened with three names: Adam, Sheth, Enosh. Your line was from Adam to now. Did you find a name in your family line? Today, the last page of that same book, and the last words of the Hebrew Bible. Day eight hundred eighty-two.

The second-to-last scene is a ruin. At the end of Second Chronicles, the Babylonians burn the house of God, break down the wall of Jerusalem, and carry the survivors away to Babylon. The text says the land lay desolate and kept its sabbaths, as the word of the LORD by Jeremiah had said. If the book stopped there, the whole Hebrew Bible would close on smoke and exile. It doesn't stop there. Two more verses come. A new king rises, Cyrus of Persia, and he sends out a proclamation through all his kingdom, in speech and in writing. And in the order this path follows, the last word of the whole Tanakh is a verb of movement.
screen: `THE HOUSE OF GOD BURNED.` → `THE PEOPLE CARRIED TO BABYLON.` → `THEN CYRUS SPEAKS.`

segments.voice: Here is the final verse, in the King James words: "Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath the LORD God of heaven given me; and he hath charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who is there among you of all his people? The LORD his God be with him, and let him go up." And there it stops. In Hebrew, the very last word is ve-ya'al: and let him go up. Eight days ago we heard this same decree open the book of Ezra, and there the sentence keeps going: let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD. Chronicles stops one breath sooner. No Jerusalem yet, no building, no arrival. Just a question, who is there among you, a blessing, and the first step of a road. In the order this path has been following, the Hebrew Bible ends mid-sentence, with the destination left off the page. Some readers hear in it the word aliyah, a going up: being called up to the Torah in synagogue is called an aliyah, and so is moving to the land of Israel. Now look back at this week. Ezra set his heart: study begins as a direction you set inside. Nehemiah said a quick prayer, then spoke. The builders kept one hand on the stone, one hand ready. The Levites gave the sense. The people learned that joy is their strength. Chronicles reached from Adam to now. And the whole library closes on let him go up. A week of rebuilding, and it ends not with the building done, but with the call to keep climbing.
screen: `WHO IS THERE AMONG YOU?` · then, large: `LET HIM GO UP.` · `EZRA GOES ON; CHRONICLES STOPS.` · then: `A WEEK OF REBUILDING.`

segments.voice: Today's practice is to take one step upward. Sit tall, as if a thread were lifting the top of your head. Breathe in, and feel the spine lengthen. Now hear the question Cyrus asks: who is there among you? Let it be a question to you. Think of one place in your life where you've been stuck in the ruins a while: something left broken, put off, given up on. Choose one step up from there, one small enough to take today. A call, a page, a clean-up, a first try. If you pray, you can ask in words from your tradition for help to go up. The bell holds the time.
Ve-ya'al. And let him go up: the last words of the Hebrew Bible, Cyrus's call to the people, and let them go up and rebuild. Today's word.
Your line: the call to keep climbing. Today, take the one small step up you chose, before the day ends. Day eight hundred eighty-two.

howItsDone: In synagogue, being called up to say the blessings over the Torah reading is called an aliyah, a going up, and moving to the land of Israel is also called making aliyah.

original.note: Hebrew: and let him go up, the last word of 2 Chronicles 36:23. in Ezra 1:3 the same word is followed by 'to Jerusalem'.

trapdoor: what you thought: an old decree from a Persian king.
what it means: after the destruction and exile, the Hebrew Bible's last verse calls the people to go up and rebuild.

what a scholar hears: Ezra 1:3 carries the sentence on to Jerusalem and the building; Chronicles stops at ve-ya'al, so the library ends mid-journey, and some readers hear aliyah, a going up, in that last word.

sources.quoted: Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath the LORD God of heaven given me; and he hath charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who is there among you of all his people? The LORD his God be with him, and let him go up.

notes: 'The Hebrew Bible ends' assumes the order with Chronicles last (Bava Batra 14b), as in the index. Some manuscripts place Chronicles first in the Writings.
Link between ve-ya'al and aliyah: both from the root ayin-lamed-heh (to go up). Please confirm the phrasing.
Editor: the ve-ya'al / aliyah link is now 'some readers hear' rather than a word-root claim, and the hook's 'last word of the Tanakh' is tied to the order this path follows.
Quotation is KJV; Keeper may prefer JPS 1917 wording.
